summary: Open-source orchestrator specification (Apache 2.0, Elixir reference implementation) that turns Linear into a control plane for autonomous coding agents powered by Codex App Server. Demonstrates turning project boards into continuous agent dispatch systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to continuous auto-dispatch theme, but already tracked by open issue HID-72

summary: LangGraph 1.2.x adds per-node timeouts, error handlers, graceful shutdown, DeltaChannel for reduced checkpoint overhead, and a new streaming API. The 1.1 release (December 2025) introduced configurable retry middleware with exponential backoff.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — retry middleware pattern already tracked in HID-167; per-node timeouts could be useful but no verified gap in AgentForge for this yet

source: Continuum Memory Architectures for Long-Horizon LLM Agents (arXiv:2601.09913)
summary: Defines a memory class built around persistent storage, selective retention, associative routing, temporal chaining, and consolidation for long-horizon agents. Identifies five key properties needed for effective agent memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — episodic/cross-run memory is already tracked in HID-188. The selective retention and temporal chaining patterns could inform that implementation.

summary: Proposes a simpler vector-only memory layer without knowledge graphs, claims state-of-the-art accuracy on long-horizon benchmarks, and introduces the 'Memory Tax' metric for compute/latency/complexity tradeoffs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-188 (episodic memory) but adds no new theme beyond what that issue covers. Memory Tax metric idea could inform telemetry in HID-163.

summary: Coding agent that edits its own codebase (meta-agent and target agent unified) to improve cost, speed, and benchmark scores. Maintains an archive of earlier agent versions and their benchmark results for curriculum-style self-improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — interesting research direction but requires model-weight access or fine-tuning infrastructure AgentForge doesn't have. The archive-of-versions pattern is too far from current CLI-subprocess architecture to implement in 1-2 runs.

source: AIDE: Recursive Self-Improvement of Research Agents (arXiv:2609.26457)
summary: Two-loop system where an outer loop rewrites an inner-loop research agent to recursively improve its research process against a fixed compute budget. Demonstrates autonomous capability evolution without human intervention.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — the recursive self-improvement loop requires a training/fine-tuning infrastructure that is out of scope for AgentForge's CLI-subprocess model. Interesting signal for the future but not implementable in 1-2 runs.

source: Rethinking Memory Mechanisms of Foundation Agents (arXiv:2602.06052)
summary: Survey organizing agent memory by substrate (internal/external), cognitive mechanism, and memory subject. Covers episodic, semantic, and procedural memory patterns across multiple frameworks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — useful taxonomic reference for HID-188 implementation but introduces no new capability gap.
